Mina / team — filling in the technical bullets below. I kept them short so we can paste into the spreadsheet. Happy to expand on any point.

1) Definitions and telemetry
- Degradation mode: sustained region-local SLO breach (error rate > 5% or median latency spike > 3x baseline for >= 5 minutes) OR API gateway 5xx spikes with >10% of instances impacted.
- Full region outage: network or control-plane loss such that control-plane cannot route >95% of traffic for >= 1 minute; typically pathing failures or provider-wide disruptions.
- Telemetry signals: API gateway error aggregation, per-model queue growth, node health reports, and cross-region control-plane heartbeat. We emit aggregated alerts to PagerDuty and also push metrics to Ops teams.

2) Activation / Decision tree (summary)
- Automated soft-failover: control-plane can automatically redirect new requests to secondary region when degradation thresholds hit (see rule: sustained 3 of 5 aggregated signals above). This is enabled on per-account policy (default: enabled for Dedicated, opt-in for Hosted).
- Hard-failover: manual approval required from SRE lead or Account Operations (roles: SRE_oncall, Account_SE, Escalation_Manager). Manual path used when data consistency or customer compliance requires it.
- Automatic rollback: control-plane monitors recovery windows and will roll back routing within a configured stabilization window (default 10 minutes) if primary recovers.

3) RTO / RPO guidance (typical ranges — actual depends on config)
- Warm-standby (models loaded, state replicated, warm KV streaming): RTO: 90s — 6m (median ~3m); RPO: seconds to sub-minute for model/session metadata; most user-visible state has near-zero delta when streaming replication enabled.
- Cold-start (no pre-warmed models in secondary): RTO: 8m — 25m (model load + JIT kernel selection + cache warm). RPO: minutes (metadata sync + eventual cache rebuild).
- Dedicated reserved pools with active-active config: RTO: <60s; RPO: near-zero because traffic mirrored and state replicated synchronously for critical artifacts.

4) Cache & in-flight handling
- Prefix/KV cache: best-effort streaming replication; during failover, in-flight cache entries are rebuilt progressively. For strict RPO requirements recommend enabling persistent, cross-region object store-backed KV replication (adds write latency but lowers RPO).
- In-flight requests: we drain active connections on failing nodes and allow in-flight requests to complete if within timeout; new requests are routed to secondary. For sessions relying on sticky routing, recommend session-state stored in replicated store.

5) Evidence & rehearsal notes
- We run quarterly rehearsals; warm-standby failover rehearsals average 3.5 minutes to full traffic cutover in recent tests (see attached runbook excerpt + rehearsal logs).

I'll attach a short timing table and a draft of the decision tree image. If Meridian requires synchronous replication for specific data classes, we should outline performance impacts.

Claire — thanks for the questionnaire. Attached are the concise answers plus runbook excerpts and an annotated decision tree. Summary highlights below (pasteable into your spreadsheet):

- Definition: Degradation vs outage: degradation = sustained SLO breach at region level (see thresholds); outage = control-plane or network pathing failure preventing >95% routing.
- Activation: Default for Hosted customers is opt-in automatic soft-failover; Dedicated customers can enable automatic or active-active. Hard-failover (manual) is available where customers require explicit approval. Authorized roles: SRE_oncall, Account_SE, Escalation_Manager.
- RTO/RPO (typical): Warm-standby RTO ~90s–6m (median ~3m); RPO seconds–sub-minute with streaming replication. Cold-start RTO ~8–25m (model load); RPO minutes. Active-active Dedicated: RTO <60s, RPO near-zero.
- Caches & sessions: KV/prefix caches are best-effort replicated; for strict RPO use persistent cross-region replication. In-flight requests are drained; new requests routed to secondary.

Attachments included: Meridian_DR_Questions.xlsx (we populated the answers), redwood-failover-runbook-v2.pdf (excerpts), degradation-decision-tree.png (annotated).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Meridian prefers default automatic soft-failover or manual hard-failover for the initial contract.
2) If you need synchronous replication for specific artifacts, we can outline performance impact and a target design.
3) We can schedule a 30-minute runbook walkthrough + Q&A next week — propose Wed 08/28 11:00–11:30 PT.
